cards.text: Psalm 91 doesn't name its writer, but he opens with a promise: whoever dwells in the shelter of the Most High will abide in the shadow of the Almighty. Shelter AND shadow, friend! My last shelter was a junk drawer, and my only shadow was a takeout menu.

cards.question: Then the psalm says, "I will say to the LORD…" What does the speaker call Him?

cards.text: Then the psalm turns to you: surely He will deliver you from the snare of the fowler and from the deadly plague. A trap AND a plague? Friend, that's not a rough week, that's a rough YEAR, and the psalm says He will deliver you from both.

Next the psalm paints a picture: He will cover you with His feathers, and under His wings you will find refuge. You know that first cold morning when you pull the blanket over your head and the whole world just goes AWAY?

cards.question: The psalm calls God's faithfulness a shield.

cards.text: Next the psalm says you will not fear the terror of the night, nor the arrow that flies by day. Friend, I jump when a cookie sheet slides off the rack at night, so I'm holding onto this promise with BOTH ends of my mustache.

cards.question: The psalm pairs the terror of the night with the arrow that flies by day. Then comes the pestilence that stalks in the darkness. When does the calamity that destroys strike?

cards.text: Then the numbers get big. A thousand may fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right hand.

cards.question: Even with thousands falling nearby, the psalm says harm will still come near you.
With thousands falling around you, the psalm says you will only see it with your eyes and witness the ___ of the wicked.

cards.text: More big promises: no evil will befall you, no plague will approach your tent. And this time, the psalm tells you why.

cards.question: The psalm says no evil will befall you. What reason does it give?

answers.text: You've made the LORD your dwelling
You've moved far from any danger

cards.text: Then the psalm says He will command His angels concerning you to guard you in all your ways. In ALL your ways, friend, even the grocery store parking lot on a Saturday.

cards.question: The psalm says the angels will lift you up in their hands, so that you will not strike your ___ against a stone.

cards.text: Friend, I stub my gold base on the oven door EVERY morning, so I'll take all the lifting I can get. Next up in the psalm: the lion and the cobra.

cards.question: The psalm says you'll run from the lion and the cobra.

cards.text: Then the voice changes. Now the LORD Himself is speaking about one person, and I'd take my hat off, but then I'd just be a mustache on a base.

cards.question: The LORD says He will deliver this person. Why?

answers.text: Because he is stronger than others

cards.question: The LORD gives a second reason too. He says He will protect this person because he knows His name.

cards.text: The LORD keeps going: when this person calls out to Him, He will answer. You know the friend who takes THREE DAYS to answer a text with the phone right there in their hand?

cards.question: The LORD answers the one who loves Him when he calls. Then He makes a promise about trouble. What is it?

answers.text: He'll be with him in it
He'll warn him before it comes
He'll teach him to face it alone

cards.text: Two more promises in that same line: He will deliver him and honor him.
Then the LORD promises this: with long life He will satisfy him.

cards.question: After all the delivering in this psalm, the LORD finishes with one more promise for the one who loves Him: "…and show him My ___."
